MARKET.head: Chilean pisco exports rose 28% in 2025, with US shipments reaching $3.9 million
MARKET.summ: With aromatic grape varieties, diverse styles, and a range of alcohol strengths, Chilean pisco offers U.S. bartenders new possibilities for mixing creative cocktails
takeaways: Chilean pisco exports grew 28% in 2025, with the United States reaching $3.9 million in shipments, per ProChile.
Pisco Chile president Francisco Munizaga says the US market offers significant growth opportunities through more volume and brands.
The Chilean pisco industry produces over 35 million liters a year, employs 3,500 people and farms about 17,000 acres.

MARKET.head: Readers react to Australian wine industry leadership, AI and small winery closures
MARKET.summ: If you’ve been reading the news and wondering what your peers think of it, look no further. Our Friday Feedback segment provides a platform for the voices of our readers, highlighting the thoughts, reflections and musings of members of the wine industry. Our recent roundup includes responses to the following articles: ‘Seeing...
takeaways: Readers responded to a Daily Wine News segment called Friday Feedback, sharing reactions to recent industry stories.
One reader argued Australian wine needs reform and must connect with consumers by giving them the wines they want.
Monichino Wines, a family-run Victorian winery founded 64 years ago, is set to close amid struggles facing small wineries.

MARKET.head: Henschke marks 45 years at Lenswood with 2025 wine collection
MARKET.summ: The Henschke family is celebrating 45 years of grapegrowing at its Lenswood Vineyard in the Adelaide Hills, with the release of the 2025 Lenswood Collection set for February 2027. Following two years of study in Germany at the Geisenheim Institute of Viticulture and Wine Technology, fifth-generation winemaker Stephen Henschke...
takeaways: Henschke is celebrating 45 years of grapegrowing at its Lenswood Vineyard in the Adelaide Hills with the 2025 Lenswood Collection.
The collection is set for release from February 2027 through fine wine retailers, restaurants and Henschke.
The vineyard was replanted after the 2019 Cudlee Creek bushfire, and 2025 was the first vintage since then with all varieties harvested.

MARKET.head: Winery equipment buyers hold back as used machinery and repairs gain ground
MARKET.summ: Global investment in new winery and vineyard machinery has been hit by economic uncertainty and rising operational costs with producers increasingly turning to used machinery and repairs, industry suppliers have told Daily Wine News at SIMEI 2026 in Italy. However, this trend was far from universal, with many manufacturers...
takeaways: SIMEI 2026 in Milan drew 30,000 visitors and 493 exhibiting companies, with 30 per cent of visitors from overseas.
SRAML's Herbert Lederer said demand is down to about 20 per cent of normal, with buyers favouring used or repaired machines.
Italian packaging firm TMG and Czech closure maker Vinolok reported steady interest in sparkling and distinctive bottle formats.

MARKET.head: Langtons' first Global Live Auction raises over $400,000, beating its estimate
MARKET.summ: Australian fine wine authority Langtons has unveiled the results of its inaugural Global Live Auction, which has gone down as its largest to date in its 38-year history. The Global Live Auction featured a line-up of first classified wines from both the Langtons Classification of Australian Wine and the newly launched...
takeaways: Langtons, an Australian fine wine authority, held its first Global Live Auction on 6 November at the Art Gallery of NSW.
The 41 lots raised over $400,000 against a $277,000 valuation, its largest auction in 38 years.
A 2010 Domaine de la Romanee-Conti magnum was the top sale at $112,125, with clearance rates above 80%.

MARKET.head: Adelaide study finds global wine crisis structural, driven by long-term consumption decline
MARKET.summ: While boom and bust cycles have characterised national wine industries for decades, new Adelaide University research illustrates that the current global wine crisis is “different from previous downturns and far more concerning”. Adelaide University said that the research draws on “decades of annual data on both non-premium and...
takeaways: Adelaide University research led by Professor Kym Anderson calls the current global wine crisis more concerning than past downturns.
Global wine consumption has fallen by a quarter since the 1960s, while beer and spirits volumes have doubled.
Between 2013 and 2022, premium wine sales value grew 3.1% a year while non-premium sales fell 2.2% a year.

MARKET.head: Australian wine stocks fall to lowest since 2019-20 as production drops 18%
MARKET.summ: The Australian wine industry produced less wine than it sold, helping reduce excess stock in 2025-26, according to Wine Australia’s latest Production, Sales and Inventory Report. The 2025-26 findings “indicate the sector has made progress in reducing stocks, but further adjustment is likely to be needed to move to a more...
takeaways: Wine Australia's 2025-26 report shows national wine inventory fell 9% to 1.87 billion litres, its lowest since 2019-20.
Total wine production fell 18% to 925 million litres after the smallest winegrape crush in over 25 years, while sales dropped 4%.
Wine Australia expects winegrape prices to stay below long-term averages through vintage 2027 as the sector keeps adjusting supply.

MARKET.head: AWRI re-elects two directors and appoints Steven Weinert to board
MARKET.summ: The Australian Wine Research Institute (AWRI) has announced the re-election of Corrina Wright and Brett McClen to its board as well as the appointment of Steven Weinert as a director. Voted by wine grapes levy payers, Corrina Wright was re-elected in the ‘small wine grapes levy payer’ category (up to 2,000 tonnes) and Brett...
takeaways: The Australian Wine Research Institute re-elected Corrina Wright and Brett McClen to its board, with levy payers voting in the grape categories.
Steven Weinert, a former Pernod Ricard and Wine Australia executive, was appointed director and will chair the audit committee from 1 November 2026.
Trish Giannini and Sarah Courtney leave the board, with Courtney resigning to seek preselection as a Liberal Senate candidate.

MARKET.head: French wine imports to China jump in September, led by cheaper 2024 Bordeaux
MARKET.summ: China’s imports of French wine surged in September 2026, with their value rising nearly 130% from August and volume almost doubling
takeaways: China imported 4.44 million litres of French wine worth US$73.69 million in September 2026, per Vino Joy News customs data.
Import value rose 129.70% from August and volume 96.61%, putting France ahead of Australia by value.
Importers cite holiday restocking, lower-priced 2024 Bordeaux en primeur releases and tightening stocks of sought-after wines like Carruades de Lafite.

MARKET.head: Changyu partners with South Korea's Ayoung as China profits fall 19%
MARKET.summ: With profits down nearly 20% despite rising sales, Changyu has struck a deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to put its wines in supermarkets, specialist shops and restaurants and hired a local team to build demand beyond the first shipment
takeaways: Changyu, China's largest wine producer, signed a strategic deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to sell its wines there.
Changyu's first nine months of 2026 showed revenue up 6.51% to RMB 2.254 billion but net profit down 19.25% to RMB 151 million.
South Korea imported 27.07 million kilograms of wine worth US$214.78 million in the first half of 2026, with volume down 3.18%.

MARKET.head: Fungus-resistant grape varieties cut Apulian table grape protection costs 55%
MARKET.summ: Towards Sustainable Viticulture: Cost Savings and Reduced Chemical Use through Fungus-Resistant Grapevine Varieties
takeaways: Galati et al. (2026) found fungus-resistant grapevine varieties cut Apulian table grape plant protection costs by 55%.
Adopting these varieties raised Extended Gross Margins by 7%, 8% without reducing gross revenues, per the study in Wine Economics and Policy.
The same switch also lowered cost variability for growers.

MARKET.head: Sonoma regenerative vineyards match conventional returns over 30 years if yields hold
MARKET.summ: Economic viability of regenerative viticulture in Sonoma County, California IVES Technical Review adapted from Herrera et al. 2026
takeaways: A 30-year cost-benefit study compared regenerative and conventional management across four Sonoma County vineyards.
Regenerative vineyards had slightly lower establishment costs but higher annual operating costs from compost and sheep grazing.
Financial returns came close to conventional farming when grape yields were maintained, with site fit and grape value mattering.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux holds 41% of weekly traded wine value as Burgundy's share rises
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux claimed 35.7% of traded value. Burgundy and Champagne followed closely behind
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages top-traded by value.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading by value.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% and Piedmont fell to 4.0%.

CULTURE.head: Wine Communicators of Australia adds three new board members
CULTURE.summ: Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA) has welcomed Tamara Grischy, Brian Chase Olson, and Luke Tyler as new members on its governing board of directors. “Never has the role of wine communication been more important to the future of the Australian wine industry,” said Lynda Schenk, WCA national chair.
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA) appointed Tamara Grischy, Brian Chase Olson and Luke Tyler to its governing board.
Tamara Grischy is general manager of Langtons, Australia's leading fine wine retailer and auction house.
Brian Chase Olson founded Blend Public Relations; Luke Tyler founded Brand Asset Advisory and advises wineries on strategy.

CULTURE.head: Five NYC wine bar dishes adapted for home holiday parties
CULTURE.summ: Wine bars have the concept of “small plates” down to an exact science. The little dishes of artisanal breads, cheeses, or meats are designed to provide the perfect canvas for wine pairings, delivering a quick punch of flavor and texture in a snackable, sharable bite. As it turns out, the qualities that make certain foods ideal...
takeaways: Chefs from New York City wine bars share advice for recreating signature dishes at home for holiday entertaining.
Lei's sesame shao bing can be made by warming store-bought buns and adding cold butter, with optional sage compound butter.
Gigi's poire au vin rouge is a poached pear dipped in whipped cream and served over red wine reduction.

CULTURE.head: VinePair lists 30 wines for 2026 Thanksgiving tables, favoring low-alcohol, high-acid bottles
CULTURE.summ: Amid the marathon of planning, prepping, cooking, and baking, finding the perfect wine for Thanksgiving isn’t always the top priority. If wine is on the checklist, venturing into bottle shops this time of year can be especially dizzying and sometimes even stressful. So many choices, so little time to choose, and what’s my budget?
takeaways: VinePair's tasting staff sorted thousands of bottles tasted this year to pick 30 Thanksgiving wines for 2026.
Selection favours high acidity, lower alcohol and delicate flavours, with Riesling, Cabernet Franc and Pinot Noir often recommended.
The list includes value picks, splurges and American wines such as a New York Merlot and a Virginia red blend.

CULTURE.head: Billy Button Wines takes two trophies and 25 medals at Mildura alternative varieties show
CULTURE.summ: Alpine Valleys winery Billy Button Wines enjoyed a successful weekend in early November at the 2026 Australian Alternative Varieties Wine Show (AAVWS) in Mildura, taking home two prestigious trophy awards and an impressive 25 medals. The winery competed against a field of 700 wine entries at the AAVWS, with the show featuring...
takeaways: Billy Button Wines of Alpine Valleys, Victoria, won two trophies and 25 medals at the 2026 Australian Alternative Varieties Wine Show in Mildura.
The winery received the Helen Healy Award for Excellence for outstanding contribution to alternative varieties, and the Provenance Award for its Vermentino.
The show drew 700 entries from 204 exhibitors across 63 wine regions and 111 grape varieties.

SCIENCE.head: SWR benchmarks 40+ wine sustainability standards, finds gaps in labour and packaging
SCIENCE.summ: (5 min read) Over the past three years, SWR has embarked on the mammoth process of benchmarking the more than 40 sustainability standards that exist globally in wine. Mammoth because the documentation of a standard can easily surpass 1500 pages of documents. The rationale for this when we started was simple.
takeaways: SWR spent three years benchmarking more than 40 global wine sustainability standards using its Global Reference Framework.
The framework scores standards across 39 topics, and the OIV is using it as the basis for its revised definition of wine sustainability.
Packaging and logistics are the most widely neglected areas, while labour issues remain contentious and are often left to national law.

SCIENCE.head: Biochar in vineyard soils: a review of yield and carbon storage effects
SCIENCE.summ: The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
takeaways: Leonel J.R. Nunes's review, published in Science of The Total Environment in November 2026, examines biochar use in vineyard soils.
The paper assesses how biochar affects vineyard productivity and its potential for carbon capture and sequestration.

SCIENCE.head: Review assesses tools for keeping dry-farmed vineyards resilient to water stress
SCIENCE.summ: The study provides a narrative and critical literature review evaluating the physiological, agronomic, and practical tools available to enhance vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions, and analyzes grapevine strategies for managing water stress. Published by Poni et al 2026 in Agronomy, MDPI Headline Findings Results
takeaways: Poni et al. (2026, Agronomy, MDPI) published a narrative and critical review of tools to make dry-farmed vineyards resilient.
The review evaluates physiological and agronomic strategies for grapevines to manage water stress under rising, erratic rainfall.
Related work cited pairs winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant to sustain rainfed viticulture.

SCIENCE.head: Winter cover crops plus foliar microbial spray match tilled Syrah yields in Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Pairing winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant supports sustainable rainfed viticulture through complementary soil and plant pathways, boosting soil nutrient enzymes while keeping yields and juice traits competitive or improved
takeaways: A 2020-2021 rainfed organic Syrah trial in southern Spain compared tillage with winter-spring cover crops.
Cover crops raised soil nutrient enzyme activity and decomposition potential, per the Soil and Tillage Research study.
High-dose Methylobacterium symbioticum spray plus cover crops matched or beat tilled yields and improved juice Brix and pH.

SCIENCE.head: Grapevine tissue sampling timing and tissue choice for mineral nutrient analysis
SCIENCE.summ: WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 25, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. This is the third and final article in a series on laboratory analysis as a component of vineyard mineral nutrient management.
takeaways: Grapevine mineral nutrient status is assessed from foliar tissues collected at specific seasonal stages, such as bloom and veraison.
Bloom, when 50% to 75% of caps have fallen, is the traditional sampling time for identifying shortages early in fruit formation.
California and the New World customarily sample petioles, while elsewhere leaf blades are preferred, since petioles allow more vines to be sampled.

NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Dr Loosen Riesling Beerenauslese 2018 from the Mosel, Germany, comes in a 187 ml quarter bottle at 7.5% alcohol.
The wine retails for £15.50 at The Wine Society and £18 at Fortnum & Mason.
The reviewer scored it 93/100, citing lemon, grapefruit and mandarin fruit with balancing acidity.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Rogovila - Wine is Culture
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Celebrating Slovenian garagiste David Bratož, plus the family's new releases
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: David Bratož, founder of Rogovila in Slovenia's Vipava Valley, died in November 2025 after an illness with leukaemia.
Rogovila produces around 4,000 bottles a year from half a hectare of old vines inherited in 1999, with no additives beyond occasional sulphites.
After his death, his daughter Lana, who works a full-time office job in Nova Gorica, continues the winery with help from her mother and sisters.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Auction: The Drama, the Records and the Wines That Found Their Buyers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the drama and record-breaking moments from this iconic Burgundy charity wine auction, featuring exceptional barrels and the buyers who claimed them
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune auction on 15 November raised €14.4 million at the hammer, down from €18.8 million last year.
Red barrels averaged €28,931, up 5 per cent, while white barrels averaged €39,893, down from €58,580 last year.
The Clos de Vougeot charity barrel sold for €770,000 to Alaor Pereira Lino of Anima Vinum, and the Faiveley family's extra €230,000 brought the charities' total to €1 million.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Beaujolais Nouveau was pushed onto the world stage by Beaujolais vignerons, with négociant Georges Duboeuf marketing it beyond France from the 1970s.
Today Beaujolais Nouveau is released worldwide on the third Thursday of November, and crus like Morgon cannot use the Beaujolais Nouveau label.
Natural winemakers Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Pierre-Marie Chermette helped pioneer the modern natural wine movement in Beaujolais in the 1970s and 1980s.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Blanc de Noirs Champagnes are white wines made from black grapes Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, because their juice is colourless.
Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, is a red-fleshed teinturier grape bred in 19th-century France by Louis and Henri Bouschet.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues critics owe obligations only to those who pay their bills, and that consumers can fund the reviewers they prefer.
Atkin says a wine critic should be just slightly more knowledgeable than their target audience, not far beyond it.
Atkin criticises the brief time spent assessing wines, often about 30 seconds per sample in tastings of tens or hundreds of wines.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction notices, and restaurant or estate sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and optional images, and Orpheus notifies them when matching wine is available in its network.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain dropped to sixth for value in China, below New Zealand, with only Chile's per-liter value lower among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow visited Beijing and was set for Guangzhou on November 6, featuring value wines from DCOOP, Ayuso and Piqueras.
